Name: KLCC Park (New Year's Eve fireworks)
Description: KL rings in the New Year with fireworks over the Petronas Towers, a countdown in KLCC Park, a light show and parties around Bukit Bintang and KL Tower. Last year's (2025/26) events included Rhythm of KLCC, a 10-minute fireworks show at Pavilion and a KL Tower countdown.

Name: KL Forest Eco Park
Description: Malaysia's oldest protected forest (gazetted 1906), a patch of real rainforest in the middle of the city. A canopy walkway of suspended bridges runs through the treetops with glimpses of KL Tower and the skyscrapers, and short trails lead past giant trees and macaque troops.

Name: Brickfields (Little India)
Description: KL's most vibrant Indian quarter: banana-leaf rice restaurants, flower-garland stalls and Tamil music along Jalan Tun Sambanthan. Within a few blocks are the Sri Kandaswamy Kovil (a Sri Lankan Tamil temple), the Buddhist Maha Vihara (founded 1894) and old churches, showing KL's many faiths side by side.

Name: TRX City Park
Description: A 10-acre landscaped park on the roof of The Exchange TRX mall, opened in late 2023, with lawns, water features and walking paths. From here the new skyline towers over you: Exchange 106 right above and Merdeka 118 in the distance.

Name: Bako National Park
Description: A relaxed riverside city with a white-rajah history, Chinese temples and colonial forts. From here you can see semi-wild orangutans at Semenggoh, hike the coastal jungle of Bako National Park to spot proboscis monkeys, and visit a Bidayuh longhouse at Annah Rais.

Name: George Town, Penang
Description: A UNESCO-listed trading port of Chinese clan houses, Peranakan mansions, mosques, Hindu temples and colonial streets, all walkable. Explore the Khoo Kongsi clan temple and the clan jetties on stilts, eat at the hawker stalls (Penang is Malaysia's food capital), ride the funicular up Penang Hill and visit the huge Kek Lok Si temple.

Name: Kuching waterfront
Description: A relaxed riverside city with a white-rajah history, Chinese temples and colonial forts. From here you can see semi-wild orangutans at Semenggoh, hike the coastal jungle of Bako National Park to spot proboscis monkeys, and visit a Bidayuh longhouse at Annah Rais.

Name: Old Kuala Lumpur Railway Station
Description: A 1910 Indo-Saracenic railway station of white domes, minarets and arches, facing the equally ornate KTM headquarters across the road. The front was restored in 2026 and the government has just announced a fuller restoration for tourism; it is still a working Komuter stop, so you can wander the old platforms.

Name: Pulau Ketam
Description: A Chinese fishing village built on stilts over mangrove mudflats, reached by a 30-45 minute ferry from Port Klang. Walk the plank lanes past colourful houses and temples, rent a bicycle and eat a seafood lunch of crab and chilli prawns.

Name: Puncak Alop
Description: A hilltop viewpoint above the old Ampang Lookout that reopened in March 2026 after a full redevelopment. The main platform, Puncak Hauz, looks across the whole skyline: Petronas Towers, Merdeka 118, Exchange 106 and KL Tower, with a cafe and restaurant on site.
